# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

8	
9	### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
10	- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
11	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
12	- **Classification**: Spec Drift
13	- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
14	- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
15	- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.
16	
17	### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
18	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
19	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
20	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
21	- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
22	- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
23	- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
24	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
25	
26	### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
27	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
28	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
29	- **Classification**: Spec Drift
30	- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
31	- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
32	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
33	
34	### [High→fixed] `cargo.rs` silently dropped BOM on write despite a comment claiming it was handled
35	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
36	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs`
37	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (same class as the earlier CST-fidelity fixes; this instance was missed because a code comment incorrectly claimed `toml_edit` handled it internally — that claim was true for the read path, false for the write path)
38	- **Root Cause**: `CargoToml::open` stripped the BOM before parsing but never recorded that fact; `persist()` wrote `self.document.to_string()` with no BOM restoration.
39	- **Fix**: Added `has_bom: bool`, populated on open, prepended back on `persist()` — mirrors `python.rs`'s existing pattern. Note: `WorkspaceCargoResolver`'s separate load/persist path was NOT covered by this fix and may have the same latent gap for a workspace-root `Cargo.toml` with a BOM — flagged, not verified either way.
40	- **Fix Status**: fixed (for `CargoToml` directly; `WorkspaceCargoResolver` unverified).

42	### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
43	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
44	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
45	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
46	- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
47	- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
48	- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.

50	### [High→fixed] `callisto add --dry-run` didn't apply `--dry-run` at all — wrote to disk anyway
51	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (live-tested pre- and post-fix against the built CLI, both text and JSON output formats)
52	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs`
53	- **Classification**: Unchecked Flag (same class as the original, already-fixed `version --dry-run` bug — recurred in a sibling command)
54	- **Fix**: computes and reports the would-be changeset content/path (both output formats) without calling `atomic_write`/`create_dir_all` when `global.dry_run` is set.
55	- **Fix Status**: fixed.

58	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04

60	- **Classification**: UX / Missing Feature

66	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`
67	- **Fix**: `Io` converted to a struct variant carrying the failing path (with a manual `From<std::io::Error>` preserving `?`-ergonomics at call sites with no natural path), both variants now have actionable `help()` text. 73	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap (same class as the already-fixed `tags.rs` bug)
74	- **Fix**: gix-discovered once at the top of the function; new `tag_exists` (read, gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback, mirrors `tags.rs`) and mutating fallbacks for `create_tag` (`git tag -a`, annotated, no-force) and `create_floating_major` (`git tag -f`, matching gix's exact current semantics) — but for the mutating paths, a real gix failure on a real repo is NOT masked by retrying through the shell (fallback only fires when gix was never discovered at all, not on a genuine gix error).

77	### [High→fixed] `callisto-conventional`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` param — silently dropped conventional-commit inference on wasm
78	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
79	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`
80	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter
81	- **Fix**: gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback (mirroring `tags.rs`), new `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shelling `git log --no-merges --format=\x1e%H\x1f%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]` (RS/US control-char field separators, immune to misparsing multi-line commit messages; avoided `-z`/NUL-termination since it needs git ≥2.34, above this repo's declared `>=2.20` floor). 86	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`
87	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
88	- **Fix**: same gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}`), preserving the existing invariant that a real gix `Ok` result (even `Ok(None)`) is authoritative and the `CommandRunner` is never touched when gix is actually available.

93	- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` and `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, now `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`

106	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
107	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`
108	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
109	- **Fix**: both `git add`/`git rm --cached` call sites now propagate spawn errors via `?` and explicitly check `output.success()`, returning `Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed{..}))` on failure instead of silently reporting `staged` as populated. Design decision (documented): fatal error, not a nuanced partial-success report — grepped all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` and found none currently branch on it, so a hard error is strictly safer with no behavioral cost.
110	- **Fix Status**: fixed.

112	### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
113	- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
114	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
115	- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity
116	- **Root Cause**: `aggregate()` reuses a single `GitRepository` for `resolve_since`, but severity inference is separate — for every package, `fetch_commits` re-discovers the repo and runs its own independent revwalk + tree-diff from HEAD to that package's `since` bound. Most packages share largely the same commit window, so the tree-diff work over the shared range repeats once per package instead of once total.
117	- **Failing Scenario**: 150-package monorepo, most untagged in the last 40 commits — `aggregate()` triggers 150 separate `gix::discover` calls and 150 independent tree-diff walks over an overlapping range, instead of one HEAD walk bucketing each commit's touched paths against all pathspecs at once.
118	- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched. Note: with the `GitDataSource`/`GitAccess` abstraction now in place (see below), `resolve_since` and `fetch_commits` both go through a shared, single-discovery `GitAccess` instance per `aggregate()` call already — this finding is specifically about the per-package *revwalk/tree-diff* work still repeating, not repo re-discovery (that part is already fixed as a byproduct of the trait consolidation).

120	### [Low-Medium→fixed] `ManifestWalkResolver::build` deep-cloned the entire graph just to run the moon-declared-edges crosscheck
121	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
122	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/crosscheck.rs`
123	- **Classification**: Architectural / unnecessary cloning in a hot path
124	- **Fix**: `crosscheck_declared_edges`'s signature changed from `&ManifestWalkResolver` to `&BTreeMap<PackageId, Package>` + `&[DepEdge]` directly; `build()` now calls it against its own local bindings before they're moved into the final resolver — no throwaway resolver, no full-graph clone, confirmed by inspection (no `.clone()` of `packages`/`edges`/either index remains anywhere in the file).

128	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — fixed at the architecture level, not with a special case
129	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` (`Workspace`)
130	- **Classification**: Architectural — loads more than the operation needs

135	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
136	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs`
137	- **Classification**: Spec Drift / Protocol Mismatch
138	- **Fix**: re-exports moon's real `DefineExtensionConfigOutput{schema: schematic::Schema}` from `moon_pdk_api` (added `schematic`/`schematic_types` as pinned pdk-feature dependencies, matching `moon_pdk_api`'s own pins exactly); `define_extension_config` now returns `Schema::structure(StructType::default())`, preserving the original "deliberately near-empty" intent in the correct type. Verified via a new black-box wasm-sandbox test.
139	- **Fix Status**: fixed.

141	### [Architecture] Formalized the recurring gix-vs-CommandRunner fallback pattern into a real `GitDataSource` trait
142	- **Status**: Landed 2026-08-04 — not a bug fix, a consolidation. Logged here since it directly addresses the root cause behind 5 separate bugs found and fixed earlier this session (`tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, `window.rs`, plus `changed.rs`'s pre-existing correct instance).
143	- **Location**: new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/{shell.rs, access.rs}`, trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`
144	- **Design**: `GitDataSource` trait (`list_tags`/`resolve_commit`/`commits_since`/`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) with two implementers — `GitRepository` (existing native/gix) and new `ShellGit` (the `CommandRunner`-shelled backend, consolidated from the five hand-rolled duplicates). All five call sites migrated; ~200 lines of duplicated fallback logic removed (e.g. `aggregate.rs`'s `resolve_since` went from a 25-line hand-rolled fallback to a one-line trait call).
145	- **Bundled fix**: `commits_since`'s unbounded-full-history-walk-on-unresolvable-ref bug (previously its own ledger entry) is fixed as part of this consolidation — an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both backends instead of silently walking everything.

149	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)

# Bug-Hunter Findings Ledger

Append-only log of findings from prior bug-hunter runs. Check this before starting a new sweep so you don't re-spend budget rediscovering the same bug. Update an entry's `Fix Status` in place when it changes — don't delete history, mark it.

Format: one entry per confirmed finding. `Fix Status: unfixed | fix applied, untested | fixed (test run + date)`.

---

### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.

### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `cargo.rs` silently dropped BOM on write despite a comment claiming it was handled
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (same class as the earlier CST-fidelity fixes; this instance was missed because a code comment incorrectly claimed `toml_edit` handled it internally — that claim was true for the read path, false for the write path)
- **Root Cause**: `CargoToml::open` stripped the BOM before parsing but never recorded that fact; `persist()` wrote `self.document.to_string()` with no BOM restoration.
- **Fix**: Added `has_bom: bool`, populated on open, prepended back on `persist()` — mirrors `python.rs`'s existing pattern. Note: `WorkspaceCargoResolver`'s separate load/persist path was NOT covered by this fix and may have the same latent gap for a workspace-root `Cargo.toml` with a BOM — flagged, not verified either way.
- **Fix Status**: fixed (for `CargoToml` directly; `WorkspaceCargoResolver` unverified).

### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.

### [High→fixed] `callisto add --dry-run` didn't apply `--dry-run` at all — wrote to disk anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (live-tested pre- and post-fix against the built CLI, both text and JSON output formats)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs`
- **Classification**: Unchecked Flag (same class as the original, already-fixed `version --dry-run` bug — recurred in a sibling command)
- **Fix**: computes and reports the would-be changeset content/path (both output formats) without calling `atomic_write`/`create_dir_all` when `global.dry_run` is set.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `callisto publish`'s output couldn't distinguish "computed a plan" from "actually published packages"
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `callisto_model::report::PublishReport`
- **Classification**: UX / Missing Feature
- **Fix**: new `PublishReport` type (following the codebase's existing `Plan`-vs-`Report` naming convention) carries per-package `PublishAttempt`/outcome; `PublishOrchestrator::execute` now returns it instead of `()`; the CLI's real (non-dry-run) path prints/returns it instead of re-rendering the input plan.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `CliError::Io`/`CliError::Registry` lacked `help()` text, inconsistent with `NotATty`'s pattern
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`
- **Fix**: `Io` converted to a struct variant carrying the failing path (with a manual `From<std::io::Error>` preserving `?`-ergonomics at call sites with no natural path), both variants now have actionable `help()` text. Verified with a real before/after repro (`callisto tag --plan /nonexistent/plan.json`).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Critical→fixed] `commands/tag.rs`'s `create_tags_with_options` hard-crashed on wasm — same bug class as the original tags.rs crash, not actually fixed everywhere
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (found via exhaustive call-site audit of `GitRepository::discover` prompted by finding the first instance in `tags.rs`)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap (same class as the already-fixed `tags.rs` bug)
- **Fix**: gix-discovered once at the top of the function; new `tag_exists` (read, gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback, mirrors `tags.rs`) and mutating fallbacks for `create_tag` (`git tag -a`, annotated, no-force) and `create_floating_major` (`git tag -f`, matching gix's exact current semantics) — but for the mutating paths, a real gix failure on a real repo is NOT masked by retrying through the shell (fallback only fires when gix was never discovered at all, not on a genuine gix error).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `callisto-conventional`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` param — silently dropped conventional-commit inference on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter
- **Fix**: gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback (mirroring `tags.rs`), new `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shelling `git log --no-merges --format=\x1e%H\x1f%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]` (RS/US control-char field separators, immune to misparsing multi-line commit messages; avoided `-z`/NUL-termination since it needs git ≥2.34, above this repo's declared `>=2.20` floor). A malformed/unparseable line now returns `ConventionalError::MalformedGitLogOutput` (a previously-dead-code variant) instead of silently dropping the commit.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `aggregate.rs`'s own `resolve_since` had no `CommandRunner` fallback either — silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: same gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}`), preserving the existing invariant that a real gix `Ok` result (even `Ok(None)`) is authoritative and the `CommandRunner` is never touched when gix is actually available.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] Two independently-reinvented `PoisonedRunner` test doubles, near-identical
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` and `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, now `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Duplication
- **Fix**: `PoisonedRunner`/`run_git`/`init_repo` consolidated into `callisto-fixtures` (already a workspace dev-dependency), both call sites now import the shared version. `FakeGitTagRunner`/`ScriptedRunner` deliberately left alone — genuinely different test-double shapes, not the same duplication class.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `gix_wasi_spike.rs`'s pinned dev-dependencies were still consuming `cargo-deny` audit budget for a proven-NO-GO path
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-moon/examples/gix_wasi_spike.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Dead code
- **Fix**: spike file and its 12 spike-only pinned `gix-*` dev-dependencies removed; `cargo tree -i gix-odb` confirms only `callisto-vcs`'s real `gix` dependency remains in the tree. The finding itself stays fully documented in this ledger; `runner.rs`'s in-repo pointer updated to reference this ledger instead of the deleted file.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `apply_version_plan` silently discarded git staging failures, then reported success anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: both `git add`/`git rm --cached` call sites now propagate spawn errors via `?` and explicitly check `output.success()`, returning `Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed{..}))` on failure instead of silently reporting `staged` as populated. Design decision (documented): fatal error, not a nuanced partial-success report — grepped all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` and found none currently branch on it, so a hard error is strictly safer with no behavioral cost.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity

### [Architecture] Formalized the recurring gix-vs-CommandRunner fallback pattern into a real `GitDataSource` trait
- **Status**: Landed 2026-08-04 — not a bug fix, a consolidation. Logged here since it directly addresses the root cause behind 5 separate bugs found and fixed earlier this session (`tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, `window.rs`, plus `changed.rs`'s pre-existing correct instance).
- **Location**: new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/{shell.rs, access.rs}`, trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`
- **Design**: `GitDataSource` trait (`list_tags`/`resolve_commit`/`commits_since`/`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) with two implementers — `GitRepository` (existing native/gix) and new `ShellGit` (the `CommandRunner`-shelled backend, consolidated from the five hand-rolled duplicates). New `GitAccess` is the selection layer: `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` tries gix once, applies **asymmetric fallback policy** — reads retry through the shell on any native error, but write ops (`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) are authoritative once gix is discovered and never masked by a shell retry, preserving the exact invariant `commands/tag.rs`'s original fix established. - **Bundled fix**: `commits_since`'s unbounded-full-history-walk-on-unresolvable-ref bug (previously its own ledger entry) is fixed as part of this consolidation — an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both backends instead of silently walking everything.

### [Critical→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam is a native-process stub — gix-in-WASM spike ruled out as a fix, host-exec bridge landed
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). A dedicated spike investigated whether gitoxide's low-level crates could instead read the repo natively from inside the guest (moon does grant a real WASI preopen at `/workspace`) — **NO-GO**: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all read object/index content via `memmap2::Mmap` unconditionally; `memmap2` has no `wasm32-wasip1` backend and its stub returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` at runtime. Ref *names* resolve (loose refs use plain `std::fs`), but no object content is readable — confirmed via a real wasmtime run against a real fixture repo, not just static analysis.
- **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. Verified with genuine black-box coverage: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` builds the actual `.wasm`, loads it into a real wasmtime-backed Extism sandbox via `moon_pdk_test_utils`, and drives real `register_extension`/`execute_extension` wire calls — not just a type-check.
- **Follow-on bug found and fixed during final verification**: the fix's `Cargo.toml` initially declared `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` unconditionally, which made `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` (native, macOS) also attempt a **native** cdylib build/link whenever the `pdk` feature was on, failing on extism-pdk's WASM-host-only import symbols (`_alloc`, `_input_length`, etc. — undefined for native linking). Fixed by removing `crate-type` from the manifest entirely and instead requesting `--crate-type cdylib` explicitly only where the wasm artifact is actually needed (`just wasm-check`, the test's self-bootstrap build) via `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`.
- **Also found and fixed during final verification**: `moon_pdk_test_utils`'s test-only dependency chain (`warpgate` → `extism` host crate → `wasmtime 41.0.4`) carries several open RUSTSEC advisories (sandbox-escape/miscompile class) plus one unmaintained-crate warning, none of which ship in the production `.wasm` artifact (only the lightweight guest-side `warpgate_pdk` does, which is unaffected). Scoped, documented `[advisories] ignore` added to `deny.toml` for these specific IDs — flagged there as **unstable across consecutive runs** (the RustSec advisory-db itself appears to be actively updated mid-session), so this list may need to grow again on a future CI run.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→mostly fixed] `PublishOrchestrator`/`RegistryClient` wired into a real `callisto publish` command; `.github` cutover still pending
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, orchestrator wiring fixed 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`, new `callisto publish` CLI command

New `SubprocessRegistryClient` wraps `cargo publish`/`npm view`+`npm publish`/`twine upload --skip-existing` via `CommandRunner`, classifying each tool's own bounded output (already-published / rate-limited / auth-failed / other) as the single source of truth per ecosystem — deliberately avoiding a side-channel registry-protocol reimplementation (e.g. no crates.io sparse-index HTTP check) that would itself become a moving target. ## Fixed — 2026-08-04 batch (PEP 440, native git-on-gix unification, moon protocol types, publish orchestrator)

- **PEP 440 post+dev combined bump produced a version lower than the input** — `bump.rs`'s `finalize_in_place` condition only checked `is_dev()`, never `is_post()`; a version like `1.2.3.post1.dev1` (which PEP 440 ranks above `1.2.3`) incorrectly finalized to `1.2.3` on a Patch bump. Fixed to only finalize-in-place when there's no post segment.
- **PEP 440 non-canonical input broke `Eq`/`Hash`** — `Version` stored the caller's literal `raw` string instead of canonical form; `1.0.0-alpha1` and `1.0.0a1` compared equal via `.compare()` but not via `==`/`Hash`. Fixed by normalizing `raw` to `pep440_rs`'s canonical rendering on parse.
- **Git-access inconsistency (gix vs. shelling to the `git` binary)** — `aggregate.rs`'s tag-to-SHA resolution and `callisto-conventional`'s pathspec-scoped commit log both shelled to `git` via `CommandRunner`, inconsistent with `callisto-vcs`'s native `gix` usage everywhere else. - **CST fidelity**: `CargoToml::open` now strips BOM (defense-in-depth; `toml_edit` 0.22.27 already handled it internally); `PyprojectToml` now fingerprints and restores BOM/CRLF on write, mirroring npm.rs; `write_dependency`'s inline-table/full-table branches now clone/reapply decor.
- **Changelog crash-safety**: local `atomic_write` in `callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` replaced with the canonical `callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write`.
- **4x redundant manifest reads** — now cached across the three read-only open sites (discovery/`publish_targets`/`iter_dependencies`/`base_versions`); the write-open path was deliberately left uncached per the scoped design.
- **npm dirty in-memory state on error** — `update_dependency_spec` no longer mutates `overrides`/`resolutions` before validating the target exists.

Review of PR #202 (fix/release-rerun-after-failed-push). I found one high-severity defect, one medium defect that contradicts ADR 9 and REL-RERUN-02, and several lower-severity ones.

**Method.** I confirmed everything below by reading code in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/w2-sys-retry`, and ran nothing. The Bash tool refused every command, saying my session is isolated in a different worktree. I could not run `git diff origin/main...HEAD` or any test, so I read the post-PR files directly. `../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` has nothing relevant, so nothing here repeats it.

## 1. HIGH: rerun after a failed first-tag push hard-fails when the dependency is untagged (CONFIRMED by reading, not run)

**Locations**
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/local.rs:105-127` (`incomplete_tagged_releases`)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:193`, `:569-612` (`require_dependencies_selected`)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:350-411` and `canonical_operation_order` (op ordering)
- `crates/callisto-model/src/release/operation.rs:330-337` (`Ord` on operation ids)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:278-308` (`releases_tagged_at`)

**Root cause.** `incomplete_tagged_releases` derives an intent for only the tagged-at-HEAD entries and propagates any error with `?`. That derivation runs `require_dependencies_selected`. It rejects a selected package with a runtime, optional or peer dependency on a publishable package whose current version is untagged and not in the decision. The tagged-only decision never contains that dependency.

**Why the state arises.** Operations run in the intent's Kahn order, which pops the smallest ready id and sorts by package first. Tag operations depend only on their own package's publishes, and the first failure stops the run. This is the PR's headline case, in this repo's own workspace, `callisto-cli`, which depends on `callisto-graph`, which depends on `callisto-model`.
1. All three registry publishes succeed. The order is model, graph, cli.
2. The order of the tag operations is then tag cli, tag graph, tag model.
3. `git push` of the cli tag fails, or the GitHub release for cli fails.
4. The cli tag exists locally, and the graph and model tags were never created.

**Failing scenario.** Rerun `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run` in that state.
- `tagged = {cargo/callisto-cli}`, and `callisto-graph` has no tag.
- The run fails with `ReleaseSelectionInvalid { package: cargo/callisto-graph, reason: DependencyNotSelected }`, E169 "select it too".
- `--package cargo/callisto-graph` does not help, because `plan_workspace_release` (`local.rs:135`) calls `incomplete_tagged_releases` before applying the selections.
- Before the PR the rerun skipped cli and released graph and model, so the PR makes this state worse. It affects every workspace where a dependent sorts alphabetically before its dependency and has a workspace runtime edge. It also hits a GitHub release or forge-publish failure for the first-sorted package.

**Fix direction.** Observe over the same candidate roster the real derivation uses: untagged packages plus tagged-at-HEAD packages. Then keep only the tagged packages whose operations are unsatisfied. Alternatively, do not run the dependency check for the observation-only derivation.

**Tests miss it.** The new tests use a single-package fixture.

## 2. MEDIUM: observing a tag at HEAD hard-errors on a signed or multi-paragraph annotation, contradicting ADR 9 and REL-RERUN-02 (CONFIRMED by reading, not run)

**Location.** `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs:266-306` (`observed_local_tag`). The code was already there, but the PR makes it reachable for every tag at HEAD.

**Root cause.**
- It formats `%(objecttype)%00%(contents:subject)%00%(contents:body)`.
- It returns `Err(MalformedOutput)` when `body` is non-empty (`tag.rs:294`).
- A `git tag -s` tag carries its signature in the body.
- A message like `-m "Release x" -m "more"` has a body.
- ADR 9 and REL-RERUN-02 say annotation text is never compared and an annotated tag is adopted regardless of its message.

**Failing scenario.** A maintainer hand-tags HEAD with `git tag -s pkg@1.0.0`, or with a two-paragraph message, and publishes. A rerun at that HEAD:
- Before the PR, this printed "Nothing to release."
- Now `unsatisfied_packages` counts the observation `Err` as incomplete, so the package stays in the roster.
- The executor's preflight propagates the `ReleaseCommand` `MalformedOutput` error, so the run fails instead of adopting the tag.
- This is an error, not a Conflict, so it is not the E167 the spec describes. Dry-run still prints a normal plan.

## 3. MEDIUM: `--dry-run` and the real run diverge when tags are at HEAD (CONFIRMED by reading, not run)

- **No `origin`.**
  - At `local.rs:115-117` a preview with no origin push URL returns early, so every tagged package counts as released.
  - A real run goes to `derive_release_intent_with_prepared`, which requires the remote (`derive.rs:213-215`).
  - Scenario: everything tagged at HEAD and `origin` removed. `--dry-run` prints "Nothing to release." with exit 0 and no unbound-tags note. `callisto release` fails with E132.
  - REL-CMD-05 and REL-CMD-04's "same state" parity are not tested for this state.
- **Observation failures.**
  - `unsatisfied_packages` maps `Err`, `Indeterminate`, `Absent` and `Conflict` all to "keep". `--dry-run` exits 0 with a full plan for a package that is actually complete or conflicting.
  - Example: `gh` unauthenticated, offline, or private-registry credentials missing in the preview's environment. The real run then fails with E176, E164 or E167 on the same state.
  - A `Conflict` such as a lightweight tag at HEAD is also never surfaced by the preview.
  - `plan_workspace_release` discards the observation result, and `ReleasePreflight` or `preflight_from_observation` is never consulted.

## 4. MEDIUM-LOW: adoption flow now fails with E167 where it used to say "Nothing to release" (error text PLAUSIBLE, rest CONFIRMED)

**Failing scenario.**
- A repo whose current HEAD carries a hand-made lightweight tag `pkg@1.0.0` for an already-published release.
- `tag_observation` returns `Conflict(LocalTagDiffers)` (`tag.rs:143-151`).
- The package is kept, and the real run fails E167 on every rerun until the tag is deleted. That matches REL-RERUN-03's text.
- `preflight_from_observation` (`provider/mod.rs:330`) drops the conflict reason and returns `RemoteConflict::TagTargetDiffers`. The message therefore claims the target differs when the commit matches and only the tag type is wrong. I did not read the `RemoteConflict` display text, so this part is PLAUSIBLE.
- In a mixed state, package A is genuinely incomplete and package B has the lightweight tag. The executor performs A's effects first, then fails at B's tag operation (`release_execution.rs:38-60`). A partial release and a failed exit follow, and the failure repeats on every rerun.
- `--package A` does not avoid this, because B is still observed.

## 5. LOW-MEDIUM: cost and ordering of the observation pass

- **Network in the no-op case.**
  - Every tagged-at-HEAD package triggers observation of all its operations: serial `cargo info` or `npm view`, one `git ls-remote` per tag, and `gh api` calls for forge operations. `--package` filtering is not applied (`local.rs:135`).
  - The executor repeats this later.
  - This also applies to `--dry-run` and to `init`'s preview (`init.rs` calls `plan_workspace_release`).
  - `git ls-remote` against an https origin can prompt on the controlling terminal. I did not verify that.
- **Offline or slow providers.** `retry_observation` (`provider/policy.rs:145-166`) retries up to 5 times with 2 s, 4 s, 8 s and 16 s sleeps, about 30 s per operation. N tagged packages offline means at least N times 30 s before even a preview answers.
- **Validation order.** Roster validation, such as an unknown `--package` (E102) or a duplicate (E169), runs after this network pass, so it is slow and can be masked by finding 1's error.
- **Spawn count.** `releases_tagged_at` spawns one `git rev-parse` per tagged package (`release_decision.rs:296`) although a batched `resolve_commits` exists.
- **Test hermeticity (PLAUSIBLE).** `local.rs` test `a_tag_on_head_without_the_rest_of_the_release_is_still_a_release` runs `RealGitRunner` against the fixture origin `https://github.com/example/release-fixture.git`. That means real `cargo info` and real `git ls-remote`. It passes for any observation result except all-Exact, so it cannot detect an observation regression. Offline it would also sit through the retry sleeps.

## 6. LOW: the tag name used to prove "on HEAD" can differ from the tag the observation checks

**Locations.** `release_decision.rs:265-273` (`tag_of_version` falls back to `tags.last_tag`), `tags.rs:162-192` (previous templates and promoted-bare tags), `derive.rs:388-392` (the tag operation always uses the current template).

**Failing scenario.** The release is complete and the only tag at HEAD is `v1.0.0`, from a previous template or a promoted-bare tag. The current template renders `pkg@1.0.0`.
- `releases_tagged_at` reports the package as tagged at HEAD.
- The tag operation observes `pkg@1.0.0`, which is absent.
- The package is kept, and the run creates a second tag and, if configured, a second GitHub release for an already-complete version.
- It needs HEAD to still be the release commit when the template changes, so it is unlikely.

## 7. LOW (spec-acknowledged residual)

Per REL-CMD-01, once HEAD moves past the release commit, a version whose tag is on an older commit is "released without contacting any provider". A tag created locally whose push failed, followed by `git pull` or any new commit, still gives "Nothing to release." with exit 0, which is the original symptom. This is not an implementation bug.

## Probed and found OK, or by design

- **Dual-manifest packages (cargo/x and npm/@s/x).** Resume keeps all release ids via `ids.iter().any(...)` (`release_decision.rs:206`). Tag operations for both ids render the same tag name and target, and observation is per id. I found no defect.
- **Fixed and linked groups, `--package`.** `expand_selection` runs on the already-resumable-aware entries. A sibling tagged on an older commit is not in the entries, so it is not pulled in. An untagged sibling is pulled in. Apart from finding 1 this is consistent with the REL-CMD-07 and REL-CMD-08 text.
- **Platform packages and artifact slots on the real run.** `ci_release_route` is checked before `plan_local_release` (`release.rs:64-72`), so observation is not reached. In `--dry-run` it is reached, harmlessly.
- **Prerelease flags.** Forge observation compares the prerelease flag. I found no new defect.

## Coverage the PR's visible tests miss

- A satisfied package yielding "Nothing to release".
- A multi-package dependency chain with a partial tag set (finding 1).
- A signed or multi-line tag.
- Preview versus run parity with tags at HEAD, with and without `origin`.
- A mixed state of a conflicting package alongside a genuinely incomplete package.
- A dual-manifest package.
- Observation failures producing a misleading preview.

The only resume test I could read is the single-package, lightweight-tag one in `local.rs`. I could not read the PR's other tests, since I had no diff.

**Failing scenario.** The release is complete and the only tag at HEAD is `v1.0.0`, from a previous template or a promoted-bare tag. The current template renders `pkg@1.0.0`.
- `releases_tagged_at` reports the package as tagged at HEAD.
- The tag operation observes `pkg@1.0.0`, which is absent.
- The package is kept, and the run creates a second tag and, if configured, a second GitHub release for an already-complete version.
- It needs HEAD to still be the release commit when the template changes, so it is unlikely.

## 7. LOW (spec-acknowledged residual)

Per REL-CMD-01, once HEAD moves past the release commit, a version whose tag is on an older commit is "released without contacting any provider". A tag created locally whose push failed, followed by `git pull` or any new commit, still gives "Nothing to release." with exit 0, which is the original symptom. This is not an implementation bug.

## Probed and found OK, or by design

- **Dual-manifest packages (cargo/x and npm/@s/x).** Resume keeps all release ids via `ids.iter().any(...)` (`release_decision.rs:206`). Tag operations for both ids render the same tag name and target, and observation is per id. I found no defect.
- **Fixed and linked groups, `--package`.** `expand_selection` runs on the already-resumable-aware entries. A sibling tagged on an older commit is not in the entries, so it is not pulled in. An untagged sibling is pulled in. Apart from finding 1 this is consistent with the REL-CMD-07 and REL-CMD-08 text.
- **Platform packages and artifact slots on the real run.** `ci_release_route` is checked before `plan_local_release` (`release.rs:64-72`), so observation is not reached. In `--dry-run` it is reached, harmlessly.
- **Prerelease flags.** Forge observation compares the prerelease flag. I found no new defect.
